overview: The City Council approved a $7.8 million interest-free MWRA loan to replace city water meters and passed a wage adjustment for traffic supervisors, while tabling a new planner position amid broader labor relations disputes. The council also heard extensive testimony from city and school employees regarding stalled contract negotiations and approved multiple resolutions regarding municipal planning, budget assessment, and COVID-19 information.

items.title: Approval of Records and Committee Reports
items.summary: The council approved the meeting records of August 9, 2022, and the August 10, 2022 Committee of the Whole report regarding senior tax exemptions and the residential tax rate.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Municipal clerical workers, teachers, and union officials voiced frustration over multi-year contract delays and City Hall working conditions, while other residents raised concerns about parking enforcement, bakery noise, and private-way tree maintenance.

items.title: Solid Waste Task Force Update
items.summary: The council received and placed on file an update from Planning, Development and Sustainability Director Alicia Hunt on the Solid Waste Task Force's community surveys and the upcoming procurement process for a multi-year waste hauling contract.

items.title: Non-Union Personnel Ordinance Amendment: Senior Planner
items.summary: After debating legal restrictions on mid-year position creations and ongoing municipal labor tensions, the council voted to request a legal opinion from the administration and tabled the proposed Senior Planner classification.

items.title: Resolution on Staff Removals in Finance and Elections
items.summary: The council approved a resolution expressing concern over the impact on city operations resulting from recent staff removals in the finance and elections departments.

items.title: Loan Order for Water Meter Replacement
items.summary: The council approved a $7.8 million, ten-year zero-percent interest loan order through the MWRA Local Water System Assistance Program to replace the city's water meters, waiving future readings.

items.title: Traffic Supervisors Wage Adjustment
items.summary: The council approved an ordinance amendment implementing an agreed-upon wage increase for school traffic supervisors, waiving all future readings.

items.title: Resolution on Budget Needs Assessment Ordinance
items.summary: The council approved a resolution referring the creation of a budget needs assessment ordinance to the Ordinances and Rules Subcommittee.

items.title: Resolution Requesting Update on PILOT Agreements
items.summary: The council approved a resolution requesting an update from the administration on the status of payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) agreements and ongoing negotiations.

items.title: Resolution to Review Draft Comprehensive Plan
items.summary: The council approved a resolution to convene in Committee of the Whole to review the city's draft comprehensive master plan.

items.title: Resolution on Capen Street and Winthrop Street Site Plan Reviews
items.summary: The council approved a resolution requesting the Zoning Board of Appeals forward prior decision materials to the Community Development Board regarding site plan reviews on Capen Street and Winthrop Street.

items.title: Resolution Recognizing Childhood Cancer Awareness Month
items.summary: The council approved a resolution designating September as Childhood Cancer Awareness Month in Medford and honoring support organizations and medical providers.

items.title: Resolution on COVID-19 Website Updates and Resources
items.summary: The council approved a resolution requesting that the administration update COVID-19 resources and information on the city website and pursue state-offered test kits and protective equipment.

items.title: Resolution on Data Use and Data Equity Ordinance
items.summary: The council approved a resolution referring the drafting of a data use and data equity ordinance to the Subcommittee on Racial Justice, Disabilities, and Elder Affairs.
